title: Career Roadmap · Staff Nurse (GNM)
summary: A Staff Nurse provides bedside nursing care, monitors patients, administers prescribed treatments, maintains clinical records and supports doctors and multidisciplinary healthcare teams.

facts.Current degree: General Nursing and Midwifery (GNM), followed by applicable nursing registration

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Science with Biology is useful; check the current GNM admission rules for accepted streams.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Biology, chemistry, English, human physiology and health education.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: Eligibility, entrance procedures and age criteria depend on current Indian Nursing Council and state notifications.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: First aid, patient care, anatomy, community health and communication.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Empathy, teamwork, hygiene, attention to detail and emotional resilience.

items.text: GNM diploma → Entry-level nursing pathway, subject to completion and registration requirements.
ANM → Auxiliary nursing and community-health pathway; not the same qualification as GNM.
B.Sc. Nursing → Degree-level nursing pathway with different eligibility and progression options.
Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing → Degree progression for eligible GNM-qualified, registered nurses.

blocks.label: Key requirement
blocks.text: Complete an appropriately recognised nursing programme and obtain registration with the relevant State Nursing Registration Council before practising in roles requiring registration.
Select institutions with recognised programmes, approved clinical placements and access to suitable teaching hospitals.

blocks.label: Eligibility note
blocks.text: GNM eligibility published by the Indian Nursing Council includes 10+2 with English and the specified qualifying marks; Science is preferable. Category-related relaxations and other conditions may apply. Confirm the latest rules and state admission notification.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Anatomy, physiology, fundamentals of nursing, hygiene and communication.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Medical-surgical nursing, pharmacology basics, maternal and child health, supervised clinical practice.

blocks.label: Final stage
blocks.text: Community health, clinical rotations, patient documentation and competency assessments, according to the approved curriculum.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Patient fall-prevention checklist • Medication-safety audit • Hand-hygiene compliance review • Patient discharge-education guide.

blocks.label: Government / public
blocks.text: Teaching hospitals, district hospitals, community health centres and primary health centres.

blocks.label: Private
blocks.text: Multispecialty hospitals, nursing homes and specialty clinics.

blocks.label: Ideal clinical areas
blocks.text: Medical-surgical wards, emergency care, maternal and child health, community nursing.

Clinical placements form part of nursing education; additional internships depend on the institution and hospital arrangements. Patient care must remain within training, supervision and professional scope.

blocks.label: Degree progression
blocks.text: GNM + eligibility requirements → Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing → further nursing education.
